# Vej

> Vej is the company building Pea (2B), Pepper (8B) and Pumpkin (27B). Pea is the current 2B text model, supporting decisions and structured text extraction. Decisions return native probabilities over developer-supplied outcomes without text generation, JSON parsing, or answer-token scoring (Pea 1 weights at https://huggingface.co/ItsVej/pea-1 after an approved Hugging Face access request, or limited hosted early access). Extraction is a hosted Beta capability (model identifier pea-pod-1) live at https://api.itsvej.com/v1beta/extract, extracting developer-defined fields by pointing directly to Unicode evidence spans (weights private). Apache-2.0 code and adaptations, text only.

Last updated: 2026-10-21.

## Model family
- Pea (green): Current 2B text model. Pea supports decisions and structured text extraction. Decisions have limited hosted early access on /v1/predict and Pea 1 weights at https://huggingface.co/ItsVej/pea-1 by approved Hugging Face access request; all published decision evaluation results describe Pea decisions. Extraction is a hosted Beta capability on /v1beta/extract (model identifier pea-pod-1; weights are private and not part of Pea 1). Prefill only: evaluates document plus one field per pass with native presence and span heads, deterministic typed parsing in code, no text generation. Text only, up to 64 fields, 2,048 tokens per row.
- Pepper (red): 8B model in development, being built and tested privately with companies. No public release or published benchmarks.
- Pumpkin (orange): 27B model under research and development, being tested privately with companies. No public release or published benchmarks.

Contact: [send a message](https://itsvej.com/contact/). Hosted API access starts with a [console account](https://app.itsvej.com/sign-up) and manual approval. Sign in with your account; API keys authenticate API clients. Pea 1 weights require a separate approved Hugging Face access request.

## Key Facts
- Three primitives: Choice (pick among named options), Noul (assess statement truth as true/false), Score (rate rubric levels with expectation computed in caller code).
- Test performance: 76.60% exact accuracy overall across 14,286 frozen test decisions (Choice 89.22%, Noul 91.71%, Score 51.62%).
- Paper (2026-10-13): "Native Candidate Probabilities from a 2B Decoder on a Single Consumer GPU". Pre-registered comparison on the same 14,286 decisions: Pea 76.60% accuracy, NLL 0.589; prompted open 2B/4B instruct models in the comparison at most 55.66% accuracy and at best NLL 1.134; the 9B model in FP8 (descriptive) 62.30%, NLL 1.003. Pea is not the fastest: 9.38 decisions/s with prefix caching versus 20.88 when the open 2B model is prompted for an answer. PDF: https://itsvej.com/paper/vej-native-candidate-probabilities.pdf
- Hosted Jev comparison: Hosted Jev 1.13 scored 71.76% overall on the same test rows with documented rounding adjustment. Jev returned 99.31% strict format validity. This is not a claim of general superiority.
- Availability: The hosted API is live at https://api.itsvej.com: Pea for decisions on /v1/predict (limited early access) and Pea extraction on /v1beta/extract (Beta). Text only; image input is refused. Pea 1 decision weights require an approved Hugging Face request; extraction weights are private. Capacity is limited, with no uptime guarantee yet. Pea 1 weights are listed at https://huggingface.co/ItsVej/pea-1. Downloads require an approved Hugging Face access request. The repository root is the serving export and checkpoint/ is the native checkpoint. Core development repository is private.
- Licensing: Vej code and model adaptations are Apache-2.0. The upstream base model and original datasets retain their respective terms.

- Hosted interfaces: GA `/v1/predict` for Choice, Noul and Score, `/v1/systemone` for Jev, and Cloudflare-compatible formats are live. Hosted use requires an API key, not checkpoint access.
- Local interfaces: `vej predict` CLI; `vej serve --backend local` with `/v1/predict`, `/v1/systemone` for the TypeSafe Python SDK, and the Cloudflare Clef Workers AI route. Local inference requires the Pea 1 weights and the private Vej source. Serving, SDK adapters, export and the context override require current private Vej source.
- Context: 2,048 tokens per rendered candidate by default; native Pea accepts `--max-length 49152`. Long-context quality is not validated.
- Modality: The released Pea checkpoint is designed and evaluated for text decisions.
- Research: Noul improvement work paused on 2026-10-09 without promoting a new model; Pea and its published evaluation are unchanged.

## Changes since September
- 2026-10-13 paper: published the Pea paper and its supplement; the evaluation page adds the open-model comparison.
- 2026-10-10 site update: documents local HTTP, Jev/Clef SDK compatibility, the experimental private Pea classification export, and the context override.
- 2026-10-09 research pause: no new checkpoint promoted.
- 2026-10-18 hosted status: limited early access is live, by request, using Pea’s native reference runtime. States are hosted Beta with organization retention opt-in and encrypted history storage. Batch is not open yet. Pea 1 weights are listed at https://huggingface.co/ItsVej/pea-1 and require an approved Hugging Face access request.

## Forms
- Hosted Pea access uses [console signup](https://app.itsvej.com/sign-up), followed by manual admin approval. Console accounts are separate from the website forms.
- Model waitlists, newsletter signups and contact messages stay in the private EU Cloudflare D1 database used by forms.itsvej.com. A waitlist entry does not grant model access.
- Contact messages are saved from the [contact form](https://itsvej.com/contact/) so Vej can reply. A saved message is not a support contract.

- [jev-comparison.json](https://itsvej.com/evidence/jev-comparison.json): Same-test aggregate comparison between Vej Pea and hosted Jev 1.13, including strict and adjusted metrics.
- [tool-evaluation.json](https://itsvej.com/evidence/tool-evaluation.json): Diagnostic results on workflow actions and tool call readiness.
- [descriptive-controls.json](https://itsvej.com/evidence/descriptive-controls.json): Post-hoc majority and descriptive baseline controls.
- [DATA_SOURCES.md](https://itsvej.com/evidence/DATA_SOURCES.md): Publisher sources, split allocations, and original licence notices.
- [DATASET_CARD.md](https://itsvej.com/evidence/DATASET_CARD.md): Dataset composition, selection rules, and filtering criteria.

## Usage guidance
- Evaluation detail: Score exact accuracy is 51.62% on the published test. The evaluation page reports that result and the two comparisons. Tool development diagnostics are not part of the published test.
- No calibrated risk: Descriptive probabilities are not guarantees of correctness or authorisation to execute tools.
- No speed claim: Inference uses repeated state encoding; development measurements exist; no production latency, capacity or speed advantage is claimed.

- Pea extraction: Live in Beta at POST https://api.itsvej.com/v1beta/extract (hosted extraction currently uses model identifier pea-pod-1) (also Clairic-compatible route POST /client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/ai/run/@cf/cloudflare/clairic). Evaluates one field per pass with prefill only. Native presence head, bilinear span heads, and B/I/O list head; typed normalization in code. Returns value (or null if missing/unparsed), guess, uncalibrated p_null, uncalibrated confidence, and span offsets (Unicode code points, end-exclusive). Supported field types: text, number, date, time, datetime, duration, and list (lists of text only). Up to 64 fields per request. Max 2,048 tokens per document-plus-field row (fails closed with input_too_long). Text only; images refused. Zero retention: not logged or retained. Development results (3,000 locked test documents): presence accuracy 95.8%, text exact match 80.4% (conditional on rows with gold span), typed exact match 99.8% (conditional on rows with gold span), list F1 0.399. Lists and receipts remain weak. Real-world quality not measured. Weights are private (not public). No MCP extraction tool yet.
- Hosted Beta: `/v1beta` risk targets with calibrations, alignments, estimate, annotate, feedback, given, bind, flows, effort and rankings are live. Effort executes standard only; fast and careful are not available. Beta availability does not establish quality or promotion to `/v1`.
- Rankings: Beta is live, but the quality gate failed on the sealed final evaluation for both seeds; the endpoint contract also failed. `/v1/rankings` is not promoted.
- States: `/v1beta/states` is live as Beta. An organization administrator must opt in via `PUT /v1beta/retention/states` with `{"enabled":true}`. Vej stores history encrypted in temporary local-directory Beta storage. Sessions expire after 24 hours idle or 30 days from creation, whichever comes first; activity never extends the absolute deadline. Revocation denies access and schedules physical erasure. History is capped at 100,000 code points and full history is re-read for predictions; no cache saving is claimed.
- Batch: Routes exist, but running jobs requires approved EU storage hosts, which are not configured yet. Batch is not open.

- [Contact](https://itsvej.com/contact/): Send a message. Vej stores it to reply.
- [Website privacy](https://itsvej.com/privacy/): Signup and contact data, purpose and removal requests.
- [Newsletter](https://itsvej.com/access/#newsletter): Vej updates by email.

Hosted Pea currently runs the native reference runtime. Hosted Choice, Noul and Score probabilities use temperature 1.334, fitted on 2,026 held-out calibration decisions and checked on 1,016 further decisions. That scale does not make a stated probability a guaranteed frequency on a new workflow. Published native evaluations remain temperature-1 checkpoint results, not a separate hosted evaluation. Estimate responses still report calibration_status "uncalibrated".

If hosted Pea moves to vLLM, probabilities may differ from the native reference by up to about 0.05 (five percentage points) in development checks. Served-runtime temperature fitting and separate held-out verification would be needed. This development tolerance is not a claim of native equivalence or a universal error bound.

Hosted API decision responses currently identify the model only as pea (Pepper and Pumpkin are not served). Hosted extraction responses identify the model as pea-pod-1. Native and compatibility decision results use a public model string; Cloudflare wraps it in result. Realtime decision metadata permits only modality and calibration_status. Beta decision metadata may additionally contain opaque SHA-256 compatibility bindings and documented ranking part bindings. Pea extraction metadata contains base_checkpoint_sha256, parts binding pea-pod-1, render_version, calibrated: false, and offsets: code_points. Batch result bodies follow the same decision contract. Internal diagnostics are not part of the hosted response contract.
